correctness.rationale: With H indicator for expensive project and Z count of unselected cheap ones, E[H]=q, E[Z]=c q and total expenditure k-Z+cH. For c=m+f noninteger, below-budget expensive outcomes require Z>=t=m+1, capped expensive outcomes require Z>=ell=max(0,ceil(c-delta)); thus r>=q(t-c)/(t-ell) or infeasible if delta<f. Three outcome types (H,Z)=(0,0),(1,ell),(1,t), with masses 1-q,r,q-r, satisfy the bound with equality. Cyclic averaging of omitted blocks ensures every cheap marginal; direct addition/removal checks BB1 and cap. For integer c omit exactly c when H=1, giving zero risk. Independent full-outcome LP at k=5,c=7/2,q=1/2 confirms optimum 1/4,1/8,1/12,1/16 at caps 1/2,3/2,5/2,7/2; infinite theorem follows analytical bound/construction.
